proposal.description: The saturation hold takes precedence over pwm_rise, so a rising edge seen while period_counter is saturated neither captures prev_period nor restarts the counter.
proposal.reason: After pwm_sync stalls for more than 255 clocks and then switches again, period_counter stays at all-ones for good and prev_period is never updated, where the original captures all-ones and starts measuring again on the first rise.

proposal.description: pwm_fall is handled before the saturation hold, so a falling edge on a saturated counter takes the normal fall branch and increments the counter past all-ones.
proposal.reason: When pwm_sync stalls high long enough to saturate and then falls, period_counter wraps to 0. The next rise then captures a short prev_period instead of the all-ones out-of-range marker.

proposal.description: Saturation applies only while PWM is high (the stall-high case named in the comment), and a stall with pwm_sync held low is forgotten.
proposal.reason: If pwm_sync stays low for more than 255 clocks, period_counter wraps to 0 and the next rise captures a small prev_period instead of all-ones.

proposal.description: The counter saturates at the nominal period CLKS_PER_SW (111) instead of the counter's all-ones limit, which forgets the drift headroom CNT_W was sized for.
proposal.reason: When the oscillator drifts slow enough that a period is longer than about 112 clocks, period_counter freezes at 111. prev_period (and duty_count, if the fall comes late) are clipped to 111 instead of showing the true count, and a stall reads 111 instead of all-ones.

proposal.description: duty_count is cleared at the start of every switching period as if it were run state, but it is a held snapshot that should keep the last high-phase length.
proposal.reason: In every period, duty_count reads 0 from the clock after pwm_rise until the next pwm_fall. During that window it no longer holds the last high time, and it is no longer consistent with prev_period.

proposal.description: prev_period adds one for the rise clock, so the period is counted differently from duty_count, which is taken from the same counter run without the +1.
proposal.reason: Every captured prev_period is one higher than the original. After a stall the saturated all-ones value wraps to 0, so a dead modulator reads as a zero-length period instead of the out-of-range marker.
